limitations: This is a small synthetic starter dataset, not a comprehensive or representative Persian corpus.
Synthetic material may contain simplifications, omissions, stylistic repetition, or factual errors and has not undergone independent expert human review.
No third-party sources were imported; no external source license is claimed.
The repository license remains undecided; public visibility does not grant reuse permission.
Conversation records have synthetic train, validation, and test labels, but the held-out portions are small and are not a human-reviewed benchmark.
Dialogue TXT can be read as ordinary text by the current trainer, but prompt/response structure is not instruction-tuned and no loss masking is applied.
The current byte-level RNN has limited capacity; dataset size alone cannot make it a capable assistant.
Structural validation does not establish factual correctness, safety, copyright clearance, or linguistic quality.
next_steps: Arrange Persian-language human review for fluency, orthography, register diversity, and factual claims.
Expand validation and test sets only with reviewed, non-leaking examples and document their evaluation purpose.
Add more naturally varied Persian text without inflating the corpus with repetitive templates.
Implement prompt/response-aware training with an explicit objective or loss masking before claiming supervised instruction tuning.
Evaluate properly licensed public Persian corpora before importing any external data.
Select and document a repository/data license after reviewing ownership and intended redistribution.
Add semantic near-duplicate review; current automated checks detect exact normalized duplicates only.

statistics.note: UTF-8 byte sizes. Raw language-model text is stored in corpus/*.txt. Instruction/response examples are plain TXT in conversations/, with train, validation, and test kept in separate files. Conversation counts refer to parsed پرسش/پاسخ records.
